The joint-test estimator is unstable under perturbations of its inputs within floating-point rounding.
Rounding-level changes of its inputs move its results by up to 2.6 statistical standard deviations
and those of the lower-capacity development variant by up to 2.5, so the estimator fails a data-stability requirement

Every bootstrap replica refits the estimator and carries this spread at the same size (variance ratio 1.02), so it makes up about 37% of the statistical block's variance and less than a tenth of any total uncertainty.
It limits how exactly the central values can be reproduced.
